title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Consolidated Balance Sheets (December 31, 2022 and 2021)
key_points: As of December 31, 2022, total liabilities were $203,643 million (2021: $166,371 million).

The liability line items on the consolidated balance sheet at December 31, 2022 were: Customer deposits $110,239M; Accounts payable $12,133M; Short-term borrowings $1,348M; Long-term debt $42,573M; Other liabilities $37,350M.
Customer deposits was the largest single liability line item at $110,239 million, exceeding Long-term debt ($42,573M) and Other liabilities ($37,350M).
Long-term debt of $42,573M includes $12,662M of debt issued by consolidated variable interest entities (2021: $13,803M).
Total liabilities plus total shareholders' equity ($24,711M) equals total assets of $228,354M.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 8 Debt: Short-Term Borrowings
key_points: AXP defines short-term borrowings as borrowings with original contractual maturity dates of less than one year.
Short-term borrowings outstanding were $1,348 million at a year-end stated interest rate of 0.94% in 2022, versus $2,243 million at 0.58% in 2021.
Short-term borrowings include borrowings from banks and book overdrafts with banks arising from timing differences in the ordinary course of business.

AXP maintained a three-year committed, revolving, secured borrowing facility allowing sale of up to $2.0 billion face amount of eligible Lending Trust certificates through September 16, 2024; it was undrawn at both December 31, 2022 and 2021.
Certain subsidiaries maintained total committed lines of credit of $186 million (2022) and $145 million (2021), with $20.9 million and $7.2 million drawn, respectively.
AXP paid $7.8 million in fees to maintain the secured borrowing facility in both 2022 and 2021; the facility has no material adverse change clause and is not dependent on AXP's credit rating.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 8 Debt: Long-Term Debt
key_points: AXP defines long-term debt as debt with original contractual maturity dates of one year or greater.
Total long-term debt was $42,573 million at a 3.42% year-end interest rate in 2022, versus $38,675 million at 2.22% in 2021.
Long-term debt is disaggregated by issuer: American Express Company (Parent Company only), American Express Credit Corporation, Lending Trust, Charge Trust, and Other.
Parent Company fixed rate senior notes (maturities 2023–2042) were $23,813 million (2022) versus $18,324 million (2021).
Parent Company floating rate senior notes (2023–2026) were $3,000 million (2022) versus $3,300 million (2021).
Parent Company fixed-to-floating rate senior notes due 2033 of $1,250 million and fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes due 2033 of $750 million were outstanding in 2022 with no 2021 counterpart.

Lending Trust fixed rate senior notes (2023–2025) were $10,499 million (2022) versus $8,199 million (2021); Lending Trust floating rate senior notes due 2023 were $2,125 million versus $3,325 million.
Charge Trust floating rate conduit borrowings were zero in 2022 versus $2,000 million in 2021.
Unamortized underwriting fees deducted from long-term debt were $84 million (2022) and $52 million (2021).
The long-term debt table presents interest rates both on debt as issued and with swaps where hedges are in place.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 9 Other Liabilities
key_points: Other liabilities totaled $37,350 million (2022) versus $30,497 million (2021).

Other liabilities components: Membership Rewards liability $12,789 million (2021: $11,398 million); deferred card and other fees, net $3,027 million (2021: $2,516 million); employee-related liabilities $2,530 million (2021: $2,528 million); Card Member rebate and reward accruals $2,126 million (2021: $1,809 million); income tax liability $1,651 million (2021: $1,576 million); Other $15,227 million (2021: $10,670 million).
Employee-related liabilities include employee benefit plan obligations and incentive compensation.
Card Member rebate and reward accruals include payments to third-party reward partners and cash-back rewards.

The income tax liability caption includes a repatriation tax liability of $1,012 million at both December 31, 2022 and 2021, representing the remaining Tax Cuts and Jobs Act one-time transition tax obligation.

Deferred card and other fees are carried net of deferred direct acquisition costs and reserves for membership cancellations: gross deferred card and other fees $3,380 million (2021: $2,838 million), less deferred direct acquisition costs $173 million (2021: $169 million) and reserves for membership cancellations $180 million (2021: $153 million), yielding $3,027 million (2021: $2,516 million).
The Membership Rewards liability is measured using assumptions based on redemption patterns, cost per point redeemed, partner contract changes and other factors.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 1 Recently Issued and Adopted Accounting Standards
key_points: The March 2022 FASB guidance on troubled debt restructuring and write-offs is effective January 1, 2023, with early adoption permitted; AXP will adopt it prospectively beginning with the quarter ending March 31, 2023.
AXP states the updated TDR guidance will not have a material impact on its Consolidated Financial Statements.
AXP adopted the Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL) methodology effective January 1, 2020 under a modified retrospective transition with an offset to opening retained earnings.
This section of Note 1 does not describe any reclassification of liability balances between 2021 and 2022.
